title: 1954 AHSME Problem 12
statement: The solution of the equations \[ \begin{aligned} 2x-3y&=7,\\ 4x-6y&=20 \end{aligned} \] is:

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text: There are an unlimited number of solutions

solutions.text:
The left side of the second equation is exactly twice the left side of the first, but its right side is not twice \(7.\) The equations would require the same expression to equal both \(14\) and \(20,\) which is impossible.

Thus, there is no solution, and the correct answer is C.
hints: Compare the second left-hand side with twice the first
Doubling the first equation would require the right-hand side to be \(14\), not \(20\)
